title: Why is Canberra the capital of Australia, not Sydney?

sources.name: National Capital Authority — Canberra, the Seat of Government
National Capital Authority — The Siting and Naming of Canberra

practice: Try a round of World Capitals. Watch for the places where the familiar city and the capital are different.

sections.html:
Sydney is often the first guess. Melbourne is usually the second. Australia’s capital is Canberra, and the reason has more to do with a political compromise than with a famous skyline.

When the Australian colonies federated in 1901, the new country needed a seat of government. Rivalry between New South Wales and Victoria helped rule out putting it in either Sydney or Melbourne. A separate capital offered a way forward.
sections.title: Two rivals, one new capital

sections.html:
The Constitution required the new seat of government to be in territory within New South Wales, at least 100 miles from Sydney. That is about 160 kilometres. In the meantime, the federal Parliament met in Melbourne.

Notice what that rule does not say: the capital did not have to be exactly halfway between the two cities. “A compromise” and “the midpoint” are different ideas. Keeping those separate stops a memorable story turning into a misleading shortcut.
sections.title: The surprisingly specific distance rule

sections.html:
The site of present-day Canberra was chosen in 1908. The city was officially named on 12 March 1913, but Parliament did not move there until 1927. A name on a map and a working seat of government were two different milestones.

If those dates feel like too much to remember, keep the sequence: choose the site, name the city, move Parliament. You can hang the dates on that sequence later. The useful part of the story is the order of events.
sections.title: Choosing a place was only the beginning

sections.html:
In a capitals quiz, try pausing when the most familiar city springs to mind. Recognition is useful, but it answers “Have I heard of this place?” rather than “Is this the capital?”

Before Parliament moved to Canberra, which city hosted it?

Melbourne. Sydney was central to the argument over location, but Melbourne was the temporary home of the federal Parliament.

Next time Australia comes up, use this little chain: two rival cities, a separate capital, Canberra. It gives the answer a reason to stick.
